survey.question: Stage 5 review of the Rectify PRD found 5 verified major findings (0 blocking) plus 6 unverified minor/nit items. Two majors (traceability-matrix gaps, stale Verify 'Fixed'-gate language) are quick mechanical text fixes; three (split F-9, add perf ACs for NFR-1/2/11, add a MET-2/3 measurement protocol) are substantive but don't block SDD readiness. Approve as approve-with-nits (ship now, track all 5 majors as change-requests + 6 opens as fast-follows), or request-changes (fix all 5 majors before sign-off)?

findings.description: Several traceabilityMatrix rows omitted FR/story ids that belong to a feature already listed in that same row (GOAL-3's row listed F-4 but omitted FR-9; GOAL-4's row listed F-6 but omitted FR-12/13/14/15 and US-6; GOAL-5's row listed F-2 but omitted FR-3/FR-4/FR-22, and listed F-3 but omitted FR-24; GOAL-1's row listed F-2 but omitted US-13).

findings.target: features[F-9].description; uxFlows['History review and closed-loop verify'] step 2
findings.description: F-9.description and the Verify uxFlow step 2 still said Verify requires a batch with status 'Fixed', contradicting the Stage-4-survey-confirmed FR-21/AC-23 wording that Verify is available on any sent batch, not gated on status.

F-9 bundles three independently-buildable deliverables (pixel-diff engine, hierarchy-diff engine, Verify UX/orchestration) plus unresolved threshold-calibration research into one XL SDD-candidate feature — too large for one spec. Suggested split: F-9a (pixel diff engine), F-9b (hierarchy diff engine), F-9c (Verify UX & re-stage orchestration, depends on F-9a+F-9b).
NFR-1/NFR-2/NFR-11 have no AC asserting their numeric timing targets are actually met; the referenced ACs only check functional display/behavior, not timing.

MET-2/MET-3 (rate-based success metrics) have no AC or stated protocol defining HOW the rate would be measured (e.g. labeled before/after corpus, sampling methodology); AC-23/AC-24 only cover single-annotation mechanical behavior.
FR-9/AC-9 give no concrete trigger threshold for when popovers 'would crowd/overlap.'
FR-10/AC-11 never define the dp/px threshold that constitutes 'misalignment.'
F-10 (iOS) assumes a platform-abstraction seam that no PH-1 feature is explicitly scoped to build; its L estimate may be optimistic.
No FR specifies the actual write-side contract between Rectify and the existing 'rectify' MCP server (F-7's integration interface is underspecified).
AC-16, AC-25, AC-32 use verificationMethod 'inspection'/'demo' where a 'test' would be more appropriate (all are concrete, automatable assertions).
SC-6's steps ('Review generated prompt...', 'Review crops grid...') lack observable assertions a test could be written from directly.
